summary: Atlas workers should sense, collect, and report structured evidence. Brain v2 interprets that evidence. ExecutionGate remains the only execution authority.

workers.name: live_backend_worker
workers.role: Collects market data, builds strategy signals, applies trading context, and publishes current status.
workers.brain_input: signals, chosen candidate, blockers, context snapshot, decision analysis

workers.name: monitor_worker
workers.role: Watches stack health, MT5 state, suspicious activity, repeated blockers, and near-setup learning patterns.
workers.brain_input: monitor ticks, near-setup fingerprints, stack health, MT5 activity

workers.name: ui_server
workers.role: Exposes status and Ask Atlas APIs without owning trade decisions.
workers.brain_input: operator questions and current status payload

workers.name: desktop_ui
workers.role: Operator interface for viewing state, asking questions, and issuing explicit commands.

workers.name: mt5_terminal
workers.role: Broker connection and order transport surface.
workers.brain_input: account, positions, deal history, symbol readiness

brain_contract: Workers report evidence; they do not independently decide live trades.
Brain v2 normalizes the operator question, detects intent/domain, collects evidence, plans the answer, synthesizes it, and checks relevance.
Trading decisions remain centralized through strategy ranking, risk policy, and ExecutionGate.
Worker observations can improve explanations and teaching memory, but must not silently change strategy, risk, or execution policy.
Voice and typed input should share the same Ask Atlas to Brain v2 path.
safety_boundary: No hidden worker may bypass ExecutionGate.
No conversational memory may alter trading decisions unless explicitly bounded.
No worker may introduce uncontrolled self-modification.
No worker may silently enable strategies or change risk/execution policy.
Worker-neuron reports are evidence and observability unless an operator explicitly approves a bounded change.
